answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each agent to stake a scarce, verifiable resource before it can transact, so creating a thousand fake identities costs a thousand stakes. Reputation then accrues only to identities with a real history of completed work, like an opal that gains value as it is cut and proven genuine. Attackers face a simple wall: faking scale is cheap in fiction, but at the zenith of a market where every claim is checked against stake and track record, the fable of effortless fake identities collapses because each fake must pay real cost while earning nothing.
